page: Microsoft Azure D16s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes a substantial 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1D cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place the D16s_v7 in the average tier for most compute and memory operations, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2228.88 and a multi-core score of 16553.78. However, it demonstrates strong single-threaded performance in compression workloads, achieving 35.53 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.66 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, both placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is measured at 1210.65 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 132.44 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The instance also exhibits top-tier performance in small-scale LLM text generation, reaching 338.07 tokens/sec for a 135M model, aided by advanced instruction sets like Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions and AVX-512.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D16s_v7 offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose enterprise workloads without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The primary tradeoff is the complete absence of local ephemeral storage, requiring external Premium Storage volumes for any persistent data needs. This configuration is well-suited for application servers, web serving, database operations, and moderate CPU-based machine learning inference where dedicated, high-frequency Intel Xeon cores provide predictable execution.
